newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand shares end the week on a strong note.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand shares end the week on a strong note.

text.p: * NZ shares close stronger on solid volume
* Lion Nathan weakens on falling sales figures
* FOMC meeting next week seen the key to NZ mkt's direction
Price movements at close
LAST CHG

651 +8 * Other movers - +9 +8
New Zealand shares closed the week on a strong note on Friday, the top-40 index ending 17.30 points higher at 2,229.79.
"Stronger across the board, which is a welcome relief after a few sluggish days," said Duncan Rutherford at ANZ Securities.
Market leader Telecom again set the tone, closing eight cents stronger at NZ$6.51. Fletcher Paper was up four at $2.90 and Carter Holt Harvey rose seven to $3.05.
Brokers said Carter's strength was a reaction to the stock having been oversold recently.
Air New Zealand "B" shares recovered well from Thursday's selloff after Qantas sold its 19.4 percent stake in the New Zealand airline. Qantas sold its 112 million B shares at NZ$3.80 a share.
The stock fell seven cents on Thursday but rose nine on Friday to close at $3.97.
Brewer Lion Nathan was the only leaderboard stock to weaken, falling eight cents to $3.30.
"There was a comment on Reuters from the company that said their beer sales were down...that's what really been dragging the price down," said Rutherford.
Lion told Reuters it expects to report a two to three percent drop in beer sales in its first half profit result, due on April 28, and a drop of four to five percent over the year.
Brokers said the market would seek direction next week from Tuesday's meeting of the policy making Federal Open Market Committee, which will deliberate on U.S. interest rates.
"Obviously the FOMC meeting on Tuesday night our time is going to be the key to things next week," said Rutherford.
"I would predict that it will be quiet ahead of that and then it (the FOMC) will determine the course of the market for the rest of the week."
